- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent high.
- If sentiment is negative or neutral (≤0.33), model frequently underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.
- Model consistently overpredicts in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed or trending downward; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for such cases.
- When sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.50 → -0.33 → +0.67), model fails to adjust; apply smoothing filter to reduce volatility in forecast.
- If 30d forecast is >10% above 18d history mean, flag for overconfidence bias — reduce by 2–4% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- Sentiment spikes to 1.00 in 3–5 days often precede price correction; model may overreact — reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 5–7 days.
